BLOCKING (must fix before re-review):
1. The "Commit trailers" required check FAILS on PR #4547 over range origin/dev..468b45d13: subject exceeds 72 chars on 3b62b18d0 (103) and d68215487 (76). The gate re-scans the whole PR range, so a follow-up commit cannot clear it. Fix by rewriting those two subjects (soft reset + re-commit on task/OPS-ASSISTANT-DEV-BRIDGE-WORKTREE-ROOT-LEAK-20260804, then push --force-with-lease), keeping the LLM-Agent/Task-ID/Reviewer/Verified trailers and the existing file content. The "<TASK-ID>: " prefix alone is 54 chars, so the summary must be <=18 chars, e.g. "OPS-ASSISTANT-DEV-BRIDGE-WORKTREE-ROOT-LEAK-20260804: fix root leak" (67). Confirm `gh pr checks 4547` shows Commit trailers pass before handing back.

SECONDARY (please fix in the same rewrite):
2. scripts/test_queue_and_drain_assistant_dev_task_packet_scripts.py::test_scripts_prefer_pantheon_status_root also PASSES against the pre-fix scripts, so it provides zero regression protection: it runs the real ROOT/scripts copies (CODE_ROOT is the real repo, never tmp_path) and then asserts tmp_path/.orchestrator is absent, which no code path would ever create. Either make it exercise a script copied into a fake worktree root (as test_dev_bridge_inbox_cli.py does) or drop it and rely on the real coverage there.
3. Observation, non-blocking: the `for root in (CODE_ROOT, STATUS_ROOT)` loop uses sys.path.insert(0, ...) for both, so STATUS_ROOT's services/control-plane/bff ends up ahead of CODE_ROOT's, i.e. library code resolves from the status root while the script itself comes from the worktree. That is the reverse of the "CODE_ROOT for imports" intent stated in the commit message. It is defensible (central state touched by central library) but currently untested and undocumented; add a one-line comment stating the intended precedence.

Reviewed PR #4547 head 247c0c596 (== local task HEAD). Core fix is correct: STATUS_ROOT=PANTHEON_STATUS_ROOT-or-CODE_ROOT is now passed as repo_root in both CLIs, the two new isolated-worktree tests in services/control-plane/bff/assistant/tests/test_dev_bridge_inbox_cli.py assert packets land under STATUS_ROOT and that worktree_root/.orchestrator is never created, and 8/8 tests in that file pass. Commit trailers / Runtime mirror guard / Smoke acceptance / Python packaging all pass; only the review gate is red (expected, no approve tag). Blocking defect: the sys.path comment added this round states the opposite of what the code does. Both scripts say 'CODE_ROOT first so local script code is used, followed by STATUS_ROOT', but the loop 'for root in (CODE_ROOT, STATUS_ROOT): sys.path.insert(0, ...)' leaves STATUS_ROOT's bff at sys.path[0], ahead of CODE_ROOT's. Verified empirically: with CODE_ROOT=/tmp/probe and STATUS_ROOT=/tmp/status (both bff dirs present), sys.path[0:2] == ['/tmp/status/.../bff', '/tmp/probe/.../bff']. In a real worker worktree both dirs exist, so assistant.dev_bridge_inbox is imported from the central root and a worktree-local edit to that library silently has no effect. On a P0 task whose entire failure mode is 'the wrong root was used', a comment that inverts root precedence is not acceptable. Fix required: make code and comment agree, in either direction, and say explicitly which root wins at import time. If STATUS_ROOT-first is intended (it is the safer choice, since the library then matches the status data it writes), just correct the comment; if CODE_ROOT-first is intended, iterate in reverse priority order. Informational, not blocking and not caused by this PR: the commit's Verified trailer names scripts/test_assistant_dev_packet_inbox_supervisor_contract.py, which currently fails at the drain_pos source assertion. That test file and .orchestrator/supervisor.py are both untouched by this diff, so the failure is pre-existing on dev; please drop it from the Verified trailer or note it, rather than claiming a passing run.
